newsitem.title: JAPAN: Big change in Jpn insurers' asset mix unlikely - S&P.
newsitem.headline: Big change in Jpn insurers' asset mix unlikely - S&P.

text.p: A dramatic change in the asset mix of Japanese life insurers' portfolios is unlikely in the long term, rating agency Standard & Poor's Corp said on Thursday.
Japanese government bond futures fell sharply on Wednesday, partly due to S&P's assignment of a Bpi rating on three second-tier life insurers.

Asked whether life insurers might lighten their assets in fixed income securities, Keiko Mizuguchi, associate director of insurance ratings at S&P, told Reuters Financial Television that fixed income securities continue to be a good investment vehicle for insurers.

"In the short-term, investment strategies of insurers may differ. But in the longer term, fixed income securities really are a good tool for life insurers' asset and liability management. I don't see a dramatic change in insurers' asset mix in the long-term," she said.
S&P said on Wednesday that it had assigned a Bpi rating to Toho Mutual Life Insurance Co, Kyoei Life Insurance Co Ltd and Nippon Dantai Life Insurance Co Ltd.
B or Bpi ratings indicate that the financial security of the rated insurer is vulnerable, S&P said.

The announcement triggered JGB selling due to speculation that insurers may be forced to sell bonds and to a perception that Japan's ultra-low interest rates may be responsible for negative spreads between insurers' product yields and their investment returns.
